megan: FYI did a quick Avalon-11B quant sweep (int8,int6,int4) on summarization slices. Headline: int6 looks promising, int4 shows spotty regressions on multi-paragraph context.

raj: can you paste the short scorecard? numbers + deltas pls.

megan: sure, pasted below. small sample (N=200 long-doc QA + summarization mix). metrics are ROUGE-L / avg latency @ 2048 tokens / cost per 1k tokens (rough).

megan: ```
variant | ROUGE-L | latency(ms) | cost($/1k tokens)
fp16    | 0.742   | 180         | 1.00
int8    | 0.735   | 140         | 0.65
int6    | 0.730   | 120         | 0.55
int4    | 0.710   | 100         | 0.40

delta int6 vs fp16: -1.6% ROUGE-L, -33% latency, -45% cost
delta int4 vs fp16: -4.3% ROUGE-L, -44% latency, -60% cost
```

sam: those deltas look decent. product ask: what loss in perceived quality do we expect on chat-like prompts vs long-doc abstractive summarization?

megan: on short chat-turns (<128 tokens) differences are tiny, int6/int8 indistinguishable. The large regressions are on multi-paragraph abstractive where hallucination/verbosity shifts appear at int4.

lia: any latency tail regressions? 99p numbers?

megan: 99p latencies (same 2048 token workload): fp16 420ms, int8 310ms, int6 260ms, int4 230ms. So tails tighten with lower precision, likely smaller memory pressure + batch packing.

raj: from an evaluation viewpoint, do we have a breakdown by failure mode for int4? is it shorter outputs, factual errors, or style mismatch?

megan: quick triage: 60% of score hits were missing detail (abstractive compression), 25% minor factual drop, 15% formatting/stop issues. Examples: long-step instructions lost intermediate steps.

sam: GTN/product guidance needed: can we recommend a hybrid routing policy? e.g., default int6, fallback to fp16 for long-doc or high-recall routes?

megan: yes. proposal:
- Default: int6 for web/consumer chat (most traffic).
- Route to fp16 for requests marked "high_recall" or longer than 512 input tokens.
- Use int4 only for cheap bulk embedding-like summarization? would not recommend for core QA.

megan: sample config snippet:```json
{"routing": {"default_model": "avalon-11b-int6", "rules": [{"match": {"input_tokens_gt": 512}, "model": "avalon-11b-fp16"}, {"match": {"request_tag": "high_recall"}, "model": "avalon-11b-fp16"}]}}
```

lia: operationally: int6 increases packing density. Need to check dedicated pools for int6 kernel availability. Also canary with 5% traffic, shadow 100% to gauge signal.

raj: for scorecard thresholds, i'd recommend:
- Accept int6 if ROUGE-L drop <= 2% absolute and hallucination delta <= 3% (on our eval set).
- Block int4 for high-recall routes unless manual review passes.

sam: product OK with those thresholds? will use to set rollout gates for GTN.

megan: also cost note: int6 saves ~45% unit cost relative to fp16 which translates to ~35% gross savings at current traffic mix if we route 80% traffic to int6. I ran a quick econ calc.

sam: can you attach that calc and a toy forecast for next quarter? PM wants a slide.

megan: attached quick numbers in thread (see below) — rough:
- Current spend baseline (all fp16): $120k/month
- With 80% int6, 15% int8, 5% fp16 => ~ $84k/month (30% savings)
- Risk adjustment (quality rollback buffer): budget +10% => $92k/month net

raj: next steps: create small A/B (canary) focusing on long-doc summarization slices and user-visible QA tasks. Include automatic eval hooks to watch hallucination and ROUGE on a holdout set.

megan: I'll open a dedicated canary and add eval hooks + CI check that fails rollout if hallucination rate on slice > 3%. linking here when ready.

ci-bot: Deploy canary created: canary/avalon-int6-2024-04-07 (traffic 5%). See /deploys/1234

sam: perfect. thanks team. we'll sync with GTN this afternoon and share the scorecard + recommended routing. :thumbsup:

megan: filing a follow-up thread once canary reaches 24h.
